html:
The eruption of Huaynaputina, a volcano in southern Peru, beginning on 19 February 1600. It was the largest eruption in recorded South American history.

Ash and rock buried nearby villages, and ash fell on the city of Arequipa, about 70 kilometres away, where roofs collapsed. Around 1,500 people are thought to have died, and farming and herding in the region took many years to recover.

The eruption threw so much sulphur into the high atmosphere that the northern hemisphere cooled. Tree rings show that 1601 had one of the coldest summers in the past six hundred years. Harvests failed widely, and the eruption is linked to the Russian famine of 1601 to 1603, in which a large share of Russia's people died. It deepened the chill of the Little Ice Age, much as Tambora did in 1815.
